findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1453-1465 runs runStoryAwareDynamicValidation for observe mode, and packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:325-366 launches Wave-0 plus selected commands. The same validate invocation then executes the complete plan at verifier.ts:1555-1565, so observe launches a competing validation plan and duplicates command/build side effects. The plan requires DYN-1 observe to instrument/compute selection while the unchanged complete plan remains the sole authority; gate observe to selection-only or attach instrumentation to the existing executor.

packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:127-140 creates every closure from static inputRoots with producedBy=story-closure-preview, while packages/main/src/core/story-aware-validation.ts:355-385 only validates a caller-supplied ValidationRuntimeTrace. There is no runtime tracer or canonical-full-baseline compiler/call site: runStoryAwareDynamicValidation never supplies runtimeTraces, and the only references are the type and pure smoke tests. Undeclared file loads/spawns/environment reads therefore cannot invalidate a certificate, yet selection can admit a reuse receipt; this is the false-negative route explicitly closed by the plan and makes closure/reuse evidence unsafe.

packages/main/src/core/story-aware-validation.ts:787-819 only provides in-memory shard partition/aggregation helpers; rg shows no production caller outside story-aware-validation-smoke.ts and story-aware-validation-mutation-smoke.ts. The promised DYN-5 runtime assets (quorum-submit-shards.ts and review-pass-shards.ts), isolated command execution, durable shard/sentinel receipts, and cleanup/residue evidence are absent, so quorum/review-pass commands remain monolithic and the sharding safety/performance contract is not delivered.

packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:396-413 hard-codes 10 of the 12 DYN-3 enforcement prerequisites to false and permits only RunStoryAwareValidationArgs.prerequisites to override them. The verifier call at packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1454-1465 never supplies prerequisites, and rg finds no production provider of these trusted rows. Therefore --dynamic-mode=enforce-low-risk can never produce authoritative dynamic TEST evidence even after the replay/fault campaign; it always reports full-fallback. The implementation needs a gate-owned, current evidence reader/binding or must not claim the DYN-3 happy path is delivered.

Coverage is not current at the review head: every one of the 45 must verification intents has a mechanical evidence row bound to headHash 3d65b3d67b8b1b43e185bbc2e5eaddd4e3a287ad and the prior materialHash, while the current review head is d3a9ebcc135e03ce51874221303bc87a63e15499. session_brief reports 45 stale intents. Those receipts cannot establish current behavior coverage after the runtime-trace, observe, shard, and authority changes; refresh/re-run each pinned verifier and re-record current-head evidence before this review can pass. Severity: high.

packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts:1332-1336 hard-codes unknownRuntimeInputs=[file-read/module-load/registry tracing unavailable] for every production command, while packages/main/src/core/story-aware-validation.ts:379-382 marks any such trace unverified and verifyValidationClosureCertificate rejects it. The production baseline path in packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:173-204 therefore can never emit a reusable complete certificate, and runStoryAwareDynamicValidation has no runtime-tracer/provider seam to supply one. This leaves the DYN-3 happy path and the approved plan zero undeclared runtime-input and reuse-soundness contract undelivered; add real executor runtime tracing or fail the claimed capability closed with a current explicit gate.

packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:399-498 now invokes a generic catalog row once per synthetic shard, but it does not invoke the canonical quorum_submit/review-pass flows or pass a case subset; executeShardedEntry fabricates one case per shard and line 454 declares the real sentinel observed solely because the executor echoes the injected LATTICE_VALIDATION_SHARD_SENTINEL key in its environmentKeys. The configured quorum-submit-smoke and review-pass-discard-smoke commands do not consume these shard variables, and no durable end-to-end case receipt or real sentinel observation exists. Thus DYN-5 aggregation can report PASS for repeated whole-command runs while the required exact case routing, real sentinel, and shard coverage contract is unproven.

CHK-013 three must intents are pinned only to the pure helper smoke node packages/main/dist/tasks/story-aware-validation-smoke.js and its mutation companion. Those tasks call buildValidationShards and aggregateValidationShards with synthetic PASS rows; they never invoke production executeShardedEntry at story-aware-validation.ts:398-497 or runStoryAwareDynamicValidation shard execution at story-aware-validation.ts:671-705, so no executable evidence covers isolated command launches, sentinel environment propagation, signed durable shard receipts, cleanup/residue capture, or aggregate failure attribution. The implementation path can regress while all current CHK-013 receipts stay green. Add a production handler or CLI integration verifier and biting mutation cases, then refresh the current-head evidence. Severity: high.

The required verifier-owned acceptance coverage is absent from all checklist evidence and the current read commands are not admissible: acceptance_topology_check returns inconclusive diagnostic_only with AT_MISSING_TOPOLOGY and stale basis diagnostics; pre_review_check_read returns inconclusive with executableEvidence=missing, mutations=missing, transcript=missing, and authority=inadmissible; acceptance_rollout_report_read and acceptance_rollout_check both return blocking fail AR_REPORT_STALE. No current signed full 3 rounds by codex-cli plus claude-cli receipt, degraded 3x1 rejection, threshold/membership/freshness mutation evidence, mode-invariant diagnostics, enforce-only blocking, or non-destructive rollback history is pinned by a verificationEvidence row. The Wave 4 coverage contract therefore cannot be reviewed as covered; add executable verifier-owned coverage and a current report, then bind evidence to this head. Severity: high.

packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1454-1477 correctly avoids executing a competing plan for observe, but the production observe path only calls prepareStoryAwareValidation and later records verdictEquivalent as undefined at lines 1612-1617 because selectedAllPass is never computed. The full-plan result is not passed through runObserveOracle, and no persisted observe artifact records full-run failures outside the selected set, reuse-failure checks, closure-trace status, or the primary soundness metrics required by DYN-1. The pure runObserveOracle helper is exercised only by smoke tests, so observe is selection-only but does not deliver the required production observe audit comparison.

CHK-009 happy and mutation evidence exercises evaluateDynamicAuthority only through the pure story-aware-validation smoke/audit adapters; there is no executable test that calls verifier-owned runStoryAwareDynamicValidation and proves deriveGateOwnedPrerequisites binds current baseline, build proof, receipts, shard artifacts, revocation, clean tree, and inventory coverage into the TEST authority decision. The production path at story-aware-validation.ts:722-753 can therefore regress to full-fallback or incorrectly admit authority while the low-risk TEST PASS and authority mutation selectors remain green. Add a CLI or handler integration test with current artifacts plus biting prerequisite mutations, and bind its receipt to CHK-009 before claiming DYN-3 coverage. Severity: high.

doc-code-drift: docs/CLI.md:44-45 and 915-917 describe validate\u0027s existing full/JSON behavior but omit the new --dynamic-mode={off|observe|shadow|enforce-low-risk} contract implemented by packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2065-2069 and packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1447-1568. CHK-010 explicitly requires docs/CLI.md modification, while the imported plan Sections 17-23 require operator-visible mode selection, observe/shadow full-plan authority, enforce-low-risk fallback/authority, and off rollback. A user following the CLI guide cannot discover the mode, the required --story boundary, or that no-story is a bounded non-authoritative preview. Add the mode/authority/rollback contract to the validate documentation.

DYN-3 authority is unreachable because canonical baseline closure certificates are always marked unverified. packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:197-214 passes runtimeTraceForResult into createValidationClosureCertificate without declaredEnvironmentKeys, while packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts:1342-1367 always records Object.keys(spawnEnv) as runtime environmentKeys. The certificate builder compares those keys against an empty declaration set and sets status=unverified, then verifyCanonicalFullBaseline rejects the baseline because every certificate must verify. A canonical full PASS therefore cannot become reusable or satisfy baselineCurrent, so the promised low-risk dynamic TEST path never has a passing production precondition.

The gate-owned baseline binding uses incompatible revisions and can never recognize the canonical main baseline for a Story branch. packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:259-263 only reuses a baseline when baseline.sourceHead equals args.baseHead, but :609-614 computes baselineCurrent only when baseline.sourceHead equals manifest.head. A canonical full baseline is produced for the main or merge-base content-tree, whereas manifest.head is the Story HEAD; those values differ for any non-empty Story. Even after the certificate issue is fixed, enforce-low-risk receives prerequisite-failed:baselineCurrent and falls back to full instead of implementing the DYN-3 authority contract.

Current stable HEAD 875a30aad5 is not covered by current mechanical verification evidence. checklist_get shows all 45 recorded verificationEvidence rows still bound to headHash 3d65b3d67b8b1b43e185bbc2e5eaddd4e3a287ad and materialHash da7ea3cf71e219f9b0a8ab8e4b04e817ee33469c57ffd2e50be2a2c9f6b762ed, while the runtime-trace, observe-oracle, shard, and authority changes landed afterward. acceptance_rollout_check --storyId=B-45a0 --json returns status=fail, blocking=true, diagnostics=[AR_REPORT_STALE], receipt=stale. pre_review_check_read returns inconclusive with executableEvidence=missing, mutations=missing, transcript=missing, authority=inadmissible, and acceptance_topology_check reports stale basis/closure evidence. Refresh every pinned verifier and regenerate current acceptance/pre-review receipts before the coverage lane can pass.

DYN-1 observe destroys reusable evidence: packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1642-1648 calls persistStoryAwareValidationArtifacts during every observe run with receipts=[] and a fresh empty revocation ledger. That helper writes receipts.json and revocation-ledger.json, overwriting prior signed per-command receipts and append-only revocations even though observe is required to be side-effect isolated. A later shadow/enforce run loses admissible reuse and historical revocation state; persist only a sidecar selection/oracle artifact or preserve the existing cache.

Runtime closure tracing is incomplete and can certify undeclared inputs: packages/main/src/core/validation-runtime-tracer.cjs:28-50 wraps only readFile/readFileSync, promises.readFile, and createReadStream. It does not intercept fs.open/openSync/promises.open plus read, readdir/opendir, stat/access, copy/link, or other file APIs that can load validation inputs. validation-executor.ts:1351-1362 then treats any present trace as unknownRuntimeInputs=[] and the closure certificate can become complete, so a command using an unwrapped read can be reused despite an undeclared runtime file. DYN-1/DYN-2 require complete runtime reads or fail-closed unknown input; expand the supported trace seam or mark unsupported APIs unknown.

Per-command receipt reuse does not bind the runner identity required by DYN-2: packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:288-305 never sets DynamicValidationContext.runnerDigest, while packages/main/src/core/story-aware-validation.ts:682-687 computes inputDigest with `runnerDigest: ctx.runnerDigest` (therefore empty) and :605-626 does not compare receipt.runnerDigest to a current runner digest. A receipt produced before a validation-executor/runner change can keep the same inputDigest and be reused; only catalog/toolchain/build/tree checks run. Add a current runner digest to the signed manifest/input and require receipt.runnerDigest equality, or fail reuse closed on missing binding.

DYN-5 still does not route real quorum/review-pass cases: packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:416-433 fabricates 3/4 synthetic case IDs per catalog row, and :437-505 runs the unchanged whole command once per shard with only env hints. The configured quorum-submit/review-pass commands do not consume a case subset, while :467-470 marks a sentinel only from a command-emitted marker or shard file that those real flows do not produce. Aggregation can therefore PASS repeated whole-command executions without exact case routing, genuine per-shard sentinel execution, or case-level receipts; wire the actual domain runners/case registry or fail DYN-5 closed.

The production observe oracle is partly self-referential and drops runtime evidence: packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1621-1640 builds `instrumentedOrder` directly from the predicted manifest selected rows, then passes it to runObserveOracle; no executor-observed order or runtime closure trace is used. The full command results do provide runtimeTrace, but the observe path neither feeds those traces back into closure/selection nor persists them in the observe artifact. Consequently equivalent=true can be reported even when the instrumented full executor observed undeclared reads/spawns or a different actual order, so DYN-1 audit soundness is not proven.

doc-code-drift: docs/CLI.md:917-924 presents --dynamic-mode observe/shadow/enforce-low-risk as the validate contract, but verifier.ts:1331-1333 places the entire dynamic-mode dispatch inside `if (!validateFile)`; when a supported validate.ts/js/mts entrypoint exists, execution jumps to verifier.ts:1700-1770 and runs only that file, with no dynamic manifest, preview, Wave-0/selected path, oracle comparison, or authority result. A user following the documented command therefore gets the legacy validate-file path and the promised dynamic behavior is missing. Either route dynamic modes through the validate-file plan or document and mechanically enforce the unsupported-entrypoint boundary before claiming these modes.

validate-file dynamic dispatch still does not plan the validate-file command: packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:246 calls discoverValidationInventory(args.projectRoot) without passing args.commands, although the validate-file path at verifier.ts:1792-1800/1811-1822 passes its identityCommand explicitly. In a project with validate.ts/js/mts and no lattice.config validate.commands, the inventory is empty and runStoryAwareDynamicValidation throws; verifier catches it and silently runs only the legacy validate-file oracle. If lattice.config has unrelated commands, the dynamic manifest is for those commands while the actual validate-file command is outside the denominator. The new entrypoint must inject the identity command into inventory or fail explicitly instead of claiming dynamic modes are covered.

Runner binding remains incomplete after adding the comparison: packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:103 defines DYNAMIC_RUNNER_DIGEST and receiptForResult uses it at :586, but prepare() builds DynamicValidationContext at :294-312 without `runnerDigest`. Thus story selection inputDigest at story-aware-validation.ts:683-689 is still computed with an empty runner digest, and receiptAdmissible.ts:605-611 cannot execute the new equality check. A prior receipt can remain admissible across a dynamic executor/runner change; bind the same current runner digest into the manifest context and baseline or fail reuse closed when it is absent.

The evidence cannot cover the post-875 runtime fixes or the e864 validate-file dynamic entrypoint. The new validate-file dynamic entrypoint has no current executable verifier coverage. e864d86611 adds the dynamic-mode branch in packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1755-1871, but repository searches find no task or integration test invoking proof-or-stop validate --story=B-xxxx --dynamic-mode=observe|shadow|enforce-low-risk through runValidateFileAndRender. The existing validation-evidence-reuse-smoke.ts validate-file cases cover sourceKind identity/reuse and explicitly test routine reuse semantics, not the new dynamic manifest, observe oracle, runtimeTrace, oracleStatus, selected/reused accounting, or low-risk authority/fallback behavior. Runtime trace normalization drops external inputs instead of failing closed: packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:162-173 returns undefined for an absolute observed path outside projectRoot and filters it out. A validation command reading `/tmp/input.json`, a home config, or another external workspace therefore produces no undeclaredObservedPath; validation-executor.ts:1351-1362 reports a present trace with unknownRuntimeInputs=[] and the closure can be certified complete. Preserve an external-path/unknown marker so DYN-2 cannot reuse across changes outside the repository.

DYN-5 adapter gating is self-attested rather than bound to a real adapter: packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:446-462 enables sharding for any nonempty `LATTICE_VALIDATION_SHARD_ADAPTER` value, with no registry, executable digest, or domain/case contract check. The same command output is accepted at :493-508 when it prints `PROOF_OR_STOP_CASES:<ids>` and `PROOF_OR_STOP_SENTINEL:<id>`, so a generic command can set an arbitrary adapter string and echo markers without executing the routed quorum/review-pass cases; aggregation then produces signed PASS evidence. Bind the adapter value to a registered case-aware runner and verify its output/receipt, or keep the domain permanently non-authoritative.

packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1480-1500 can label an enforce-low-risk run as enforce-authority, but execution unconditionally continues into the complete configured plan at :1582-1592 and the returned status/allPass/commands are then built from that complete-plan result at :1674-1684. The validate-file branch repeats the same pattern at :1811-1832 and :1840-1944. No branch consumes dynamic.dynamicAllPass as the TEST verdict or skips the full oracle when the gate-owned authority decision is true. DYN-3 is therefore only report metadata, not low-risk dynamic TEST authority, so the principal enforce capability and performance outcome remain undelivered.

Canonical baseline freshness still ignores runner/toolchain identity: packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:638-645 defines baselineCurrent from sourceHead, inventory/catalog digests, and epoch only; packages/main/src/core/story-aware-validation.ts:427-434 verifies the baseline signature/expiry but never compares runnerDigest or toolchainDigest to the current executor. An old signed canonical baseline remains gate-current after runner or toolchain changes, so its closure/receipts can authorize dynamic evidence against a changed execution environment. Bind current runner/toolchain digests into baselineCurrent and the baseline verifier, or fail authority closed.

packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:434-447 still manufactures three or four synthetic case IDs and treats any nonempty LATTICE_VALIDATION_SHARD_ADAPTER value as sufficient wiring. Lines :493-508 then accept runner-authored PROOF_OR_STOP_CASES and PROOF_OR_STOP_SENTINEL strings as proof of exact routing, without a canonical quorum/review-pass case registry or case-level results. packages/main/src/tasks/story-aware-validation-production-smoke.ts:31-40 demonstrates the accepted adapter is only a node command that echoes those supplied environment values; it executes no real quorum or review-pass cases yet the aggregate passes. The missing-adapter path now fails closed, but a self-attesting echo adapter can still mint PASS, so DYN-5 exact routing and genuine sentinel execution remain fail-open.

Observe now checks whether full-plan results emitted a `spawn` event, but still does not persist or compare the actual runtime closure: packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1625-1644 reduces each command trace to events/unknownRuntimeInputs only, and runObserveOracle receives only the result-array order. readPaths/loadedPaths/spawnedPaths/environmentKeys from the executor are not fed into the manifest closure certificates or the persisted observe report, so an undeclared runtime input observed during the full oracle is not surfaced as an observe mismatch/invalid reuse candidate. The validate-file branch at :1842-1870 omits even this trace summary. DYN-1 requires closure-trace audit evidence, not only a spawn-presence check.

packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:441-560 still treats DYN-5 adapter identity as a name-to-constant digest and accepts stdout markers after only observing a registry read; an arbitrary command can read LATTICE_VALIDATION_SHARD_CASE_REGISTRY and echo the exact PROOF_OR_STOP_CASES/SENTINEL markers without executing any registered case or real domain runner. The production smoke at packages/main/src/tasks/story-aware-validation-production-smoke.ts:26-43 demonstrates this generic echo command is accepted. Bind the adapter to a registered executable/implementation digest and case-level execution receipt, or keep DYN-5 non-authoritative.

packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1674-1716 and 1983-2020 now append full-oracle runtimeTrace fields to a human/report string, but do not pass those observations through runtimeTraceForResult/createValidationClosureCertificate, invalidate the affected closure, or revoke existing receipts. A full oracle can therefore observe a new undeclared read/spawn/environment access while the next dynamic run still admits the old reusable receipt; trace visibility is not closure/reuse enforcement. Feed the full oracle trace into closure certification and fail closed on undeclared inputs.

At current HEAD 70043236d1, all 45 checklist verificationEvidence rows remain bound to old headHash 3d65b3d67b8b1b43e185bbc2e5eaddd4e3a287ad and materialHash da7ea3cf71e219f9b0a8ab8e4b04e817ee33469c57ffd2e50be2a2c9f6b762ed. acceptance_rollout_check is blocking with AR_REPORT_STALE and stale receipt; pre_review_check_read is inconclusive with executableEvidence, mutations, and transcript missing and authority inadmissible; acceptance_topology_check is inconclusive with stale basis and missing topology. The new validate-file preview and registry-backed shard code therefore has no admissible current acceptance evidence. Refresh current-head checklist evidence and reissue rollout, pre-review, and topology receipts before coverage can pass.

The current validate-file dynamic entrypoint is not covered end to end for a story-scoped invocation. validation-protocol-smoke.ts now exercises only a no-story dynamic preview with dynamicMode observe, commandExecutions 0, oracleStatus not-run, and a synthetic one-file manifest. No current smoke or verification evidence invokes validate-file with storyId and dynamicMode observe, shadow, or enforce-low-risk to assert story-aware manifest binding, runtime trace, authority versus fallback, authoritativeResult, or oracle equivalence. The implementation branch in verifier.ts can therefore regress while all current smoke tests remain green. Add executable story-scoped validate-file coverage for observe, shadow, and enforce or an explicit fail-closed fallback.

packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1493-1504 and 1917-1928 omit the live Story scopeContract, verificationIntents, affectedProcessFacts, and affectedCapabilities when calling runStoryAwareDynamicValidation. packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:268-278 therefore signs an empty scope/pin/fact/capability projection, and line 833 treats the absent pin set as vacuously executed. The enforce-authority branches at verifier.ts:1605-1630 and 1959-1979 then persist that result as routine validation evidence without the mandatory Story inputs. A protected/out-of-scope/excluded change or missing verificationIntent pin can therefore be absent from the authority decision instead of forcing full validation, violating DYN-3 and Section 14.1.

The new registry-backed production smoke is still weaker than the DYN-5 contract. story-aware-validation-production-smoke.ts runs only the review-pass domain with the case-registry adapter, then asserts build pass, authority false, shardRoot existence, and that one aggregate artifact contains coveredCaseIds. It does not assert every signed per-shard receipt has registryObserved, sentinelObserved, caseRegistryDigest, adapterDigest, zero residue, and valid signatures; it does not assert exact no-omission/no-duplicate/correct-routing case sets, aggregate verdict equivalence, or quorum 3-to-4 shard behavior. Because the smoke accepts authority false and never exercises a complete current acceptance receipt, the registry-backed production path can be partially wired while the smoke passes. Extend executable smoke and mutation evidence across review-pass and quorum with exact receipt and residue assertions.

packages/main/src/core/validation-runtime-tracer.cjs:19,70-74 records every environment key visible at startup and only the unresolved Module._load request string, while packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:221-234 declares that entire key set as allowed for canonical baselines. Thus a command reading an undeclared secret env var is indistinguishable from merely inheriting it, and require('external-package') is recorded as a bare package name then dropped by sourceAuthorityPath instead of resolving to the loaded file. The resulting closure certificate can remain complete for undeclared environment/module inputs. Trace actual env access and resolved module filenames, or fail closed when resolution is unavailable.

packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:715-735 does not mechanically prove the Section 24 enforcement prerequisites it labels PASS: wholeRepoScannersClassified is just catalogOwnershipGatePassed; processFactBindingsComplete is vacuously true for empty bindings; changedTestPropagationVerified only rechecks zero manifest counters; periodicFullPolicyActive is only baselineCurrent; and catalogOwnershipGatePassed only checks id/inputRoots/resources. packages/main/src/core/story-aware-validation.ts:332-341 compounds this by assigning every discovered command the same story-selectable/local/static-and-traced defaults, so actual full-only, whole-repository, gate/shared risk, ownership-review, changed-test consumer, and periodic-audit facts are not represented. An enforce-low-risk run can therefore receive all-true prerequisite rows without the facts Section 24 requires.

packages/main/src/handlers/story-aware-validation.ts:441-446 registers a marker-only DYN-5 adapter, while lines 552-569 accept a shard when the command merely read the registry and printed PROOF_OR_STOP_CASES/PROOF_OR_STOP_SENTINEL. The production-path test at packages/main/src/tasks/story-aware-validation-production-smoke.ts:38-44 does exactly that: it reads JSON, echoes IDs and a sentinel, and executes no quorum/review-pass case logic, yet lines 56-63 assert production shard receipts PASS. Thus missing/unregistered adapters do fail closed, but the registered adapter can mint PASS by replaying markers without running each case or the genuine end-to-end sentinel, violating DYN-5 static-PASS, routing, and aggregate-equivalence requirements. The repository validate config also contains no caseRegistryPath/LATTICE_VALIDATION_SHARD_ADAPTER for its actual review-pass/quorum commands, so the real domains are not wired.

The promised current-main characterization, operations record, and enforcement-evidence documents are also absent. This leaves the required zero-false-negative evidence undelivered while the audit adapter reports PASS.

At current HEAD 0d3491f8adbd4db4d40e189476e6df761277474e, checklist_get shows all 45 verificationEvidence rows still bound to old headHash 3d65b3d67b8b1b43e185bbc2e5eaddd4e3a287ad and materialHash da7ea3cf71e219f9b0a8ab8e4b04e817ee33469c57ffd2e50be2a2c9f6b762ed. acceptance_rollout_check is blocking with AR_REPORT_STALE and a stale receipt; pre_review_check_read is inconclusive with executableEvidence, mutations, and transcript missing and authority inadmissible; acceptance_topology_check is inconclusive with partial legacy-missing topology and stale closure/basis diagnostics. DYN-3/DYN-5 are not wired through the real verifier command inventory. configuredValidationCommands() narrows each configured command to generic ValidationCommand fields and drops the catalog's assurance, riskTier, closurePolicy, fullBaselineReusePolicy, cpuWeight and expectedP50Ms fields (verifier.ts:317-353; validation-types.ts:6-29). prepare() then gives the injected args.commands inventory precedence (story-aware-validation.ts:255-264), so the normal verifier path cannot retain explicit catalog policy even though raw config discovery supports it. The repository configs also declare no caseRegistryPath or registered shard adapter. The production smoke bypasses this path by calling runStoryAwareDynamicValidation directly with a synthetic config and explicitly expects non-authoritative output. Consequently Section 24's explicit-policy prerequisite fails closed in production, and there is no demonstrated real DYN-3 enforce/DYN-5 execution path.

The registered DYN-5 adapter is still a trusted evidence generator rather than a real case executor. story-aware-validation.ts binds the exact adapter entrypoint and checks per-case evidence, but story-aware-validation-case-adapter.mjs:46-63 merely loops over requested IDs and writes evidence with executed:true plus routing/sentinel markers; it never invokes the quorum/review-pass handler cases or any test body. An unchanged adapter can therefore report every requested stable ID as executed even when no behavior ran, violating the plan's genuine end-to-end sentinel and static-PASS rejection requirements.

The Section 19/21 assurance campaign remains synthetic rather than the promised replay evidence. story-aware-validation-mutation-smoke.ts creates a temporary repository with four Node -e commands, generates 30 path-shape classes, and now gives only class 29 a synthetic e2e failure. It does not restore 30-50 historical Story base/head pairs, run each Story's complete oracle versus dynamic selection, persist durable per-Story manifests/receipts, run FI-1..FI-5 for every applicable catalog entry, or perform the three alternating paired current-HEAD experiments. The required characterization, operations and enforcement-evidence decision documents are also absent. Current reproduction: lifecycle_check --storyId=B-45a0 --target=TEST --format=json reports pass B-45a0:RP-429 failed closeout metadata retention: untrusted closeout artifact path: checklist.json; invalid closeout artifact: checklist.json, even though intent coverage is pass and refreshed receipts retain matching materialHash/storyFilesHash. This makes a required evidence refresh invalidate the current review pass and prevents REVIEW to TEST. Register checklist.json with the correct canonical verification-evidence writers and receipt validation, then cover the allowed and non-canonical-writer rejection cases.

findings.desc: docs-closeout-retention-contract: docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md:195,265,278 promise that verification_evidence_refresh_stale safely re-executes pinned evidence and re-stamps current freshness, but omit that its canonical checklist.json mutation must retain an already-current review receipt only through a verified closeout-evidence writer/receipt lineage. The actual retention gate rejects the refresh because checklist.json has no CLOSEOUT_ARTIFACT_POLICIES entry (packages/main/src/core/closeout-trust.ts:37-49,607-610), although the command necessarily rewrites that file (packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:1140-1168). Consequently, the documented remediation for stale evidence can itself invalidate REVIEW and deadlock REVIEW→TEST without product-material change. Add an explicit lifecycle contract for canonical evidence-refresh retention, its permitted writer(s), and the safe rejection behavior for non-canonical checklist mutations, coupled to the code fix and tests.

findings.desc: Verified topology blocker: acceptance_basis_generate derives and signs binding hashes before persisting acceptance-basis.json. Because this output is story-owned evidence, the immediate topology_critic_receipt_set --verdict=pass verifies against a changed state and refuses with AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING: basis semantic discovery digest mismatch; scope-contract digest mismatch; closure files hash mismatch; snapshot seal digest mismatch; freshness mismatch: evidence storyFilesHash does not match current story-owned file state. An independent critic cannot sign a complete basis. Reproduced by acceptance_basis_generate followed by topology_critic_receipt_set; the signed critic receipt is request_changes.
findings.resolvedReason: Reproduced, root-caused, and verified resolved. REPRO: acceptance_basis_generate printed 'Receipt: (verified)' yet the immediately following acceptance_basis read returned AT_ADAPTER_RESULT_DIGEST_MISMATCH (basis semantic discovery digest mismatch; closure files hash mismatch; snapshot seal digest mismatch) on a clean tree with no writes in between, and acceptance_topology_check reported Status=inconclusive with AT_CLOSURE_FILES_STALE. ROOT CAUSE: this is a convergence property of the derived closure snapshot, not unconditional self-staleness. closureFilesHash is computed by computeClosureFilesHashFromSnapshots over the discovery source snapshots (acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:295). When other story activity has changed the registered producer/consumer closure since the last basis, the first generate binds a receipt against a closure that its own discovery pass then supersedes, so the next read sees stale bindings. ISOLATION: two consecutive generates at identical tree state produced a STABLE closureFilesHash (sha256:8e7550c8...) on both runs, proving the derivation is deterministic and converges rather than being unstable per-run. CONFIRM: after convergence the basis reads 'complete' with 'Receipt verification: PASS', acceptance_topology_check reports Status=pass, Structural pass=yes, Diagnostics none, and the previously reported AT_UNMAPPED_SCOPE_REF for story-change-resolver#buildStoryChangeManifest is gone. This was re-verified as still PASS after three subsequent finding_resolve story-file writes, showing story metadata writes do not re-stale the binding. The critic can now sign a complete basis, which is the capability F-426 reported as impossible.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/historical-replay-artifact.ts:171-172 the paired-performance-inventory-stale and paired-performance-catalog-stale rejection branches (inside checkPairedPerformance, reached only when value.head equals expected.head or expected.admittedHistoricalHead) have zero test coverage: grep for these exact strings across packages/main/src finds only their own definition site, never a test assertion. historical-replay-artifact-smoke.ts:199-207 (F-423/F-425 resolution cited producer-drift regression) only exercises isPermittedReplayHeadDriftPath allowlist rejection, which short-circuits before the digest comparisons at 171-172 -- it never causes inventoryDigest or catalogDigest to actually diverge while head/admittedHistoricalHead still match. Since inventoryDigest/catalogDigest are recomputed from live working-tree filesystem state, the scenario these two branches exist to catch (catalog/inventory-affecting source mutated while HEAD is unchanged or only drifted through admitted consumer paths) is untested and the branches remain dead code from a test-coverage perspective. F-423 resolution's general claim of producer/config/catalog/runner drift rejection holds for path-allowlist-detectable drift but not for this specific digest-mismatch mechanism. Recommend a test case that holds head/admittedHistoricalHead constant while mutating a real catalog/inventory-affecting source file so inventoryDigest or catalogDigest actually differs, asserting the corresponding reason fires.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in f2e648606d. Confirmed the finding first: grep for paired-performance-inventory-stale and paired-performance-catalog-stale across packages/main/src and scripts returned only their own definition sites at historical-replay-artifact.ts:171-172, with no test assertion, and the existing producer-drift case asserts paired-performance-head-stale, which returns at the head check (line 168) before either digest comparison is reached. Added coverage in historical-replay-artifact-smoke.ts driving each digest to diverge while HEAD is held constant (no commit), so the live-recomputed inventory/catalog digest disagrees with the one signed into the report. Reaching those branches requires a VALID signature over a divergent digest, so buildReport gained a digestOverrides parameter that signs the override in; an initial attempt that mutated the digest after signing was rejected at paired-performance-signature-invalid instead, and the debug output of that failure is what identified the correct construction. Each case additionally asserts the reason is NOT paired-performance-signature-invalid and NOT paired-performance-head-stale, pinning that the intended branch fired rather than an earlier one. Verified by mutation testing rather than by the test merely passing: deleting the inventory branch fails the smoke test (exit 1), deleting the catalog branch fails it (exit 1), and restoring both returns historical replay artifact smoke PASS with git diff --stat showing zero change to the production file. No production code was modified.

findings.desc: F-428/F-429/F-430 resolvedReason unconditionally claims 'pre_review_check: PASS with zero codes, down from ten' as a settled, current fact. Independently re-running the read-only pre_review_check_read right now (REVIEW phase, HEAD 0c61e81d0c) reproduces FAIL with codes=[PR_ARTIFACT_TAMPERED,PR_COVERAGE_BASIS_CHANGED], stably across repeat calls. Git history for .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-45a0/{pre-review-check.json,acceptance-basis.json} shows the PASS was real at commit 38fd3b206d (bound to PLAN basisDigest sha256:d42824c0...), but acceptance_basis_generate was rerun twice more afterward (5dee7587a8, 5ce0fd05ed), producing a new basisDigest sha256:9e661a77... that was never re-certified via a follow-up pre_review_check before findings were marked resolved and the story advanced to REVIEW (0e1c5a3991). Root cause: the two later acceptance-basis.json snapshots are semantically byte-identical to the one pre_review_check passed against (same enumeratedPathRefs/adapterResults/status/blindSpots, only binding.headHash differs from git auto-commit churn) -- this is the benign drift class acceptanceCoverageBasisSemanticDigest exists to detect, but issuePreReviewCheckArtifacts PR_COVERAGE_BASIS_CHANGED check (pre-review-check.ts line ~342) compares raw basisDigest instead, so it false-positives on every acceptance_basis_generate rerun after a pre_review_check pass. The harder-won proof state from the transcript repair is unaffected (plannedActual=complete, executableEvidence=current, mutations=biting, transcript=related, authority=admissible all still hold), and this gate is non-blocking in current observe mode, so nothing is silently bypassed -- but the finding_resolve text overclaims a currently-false PASS as fact, which is a documentation/evidence-honesty gap the next reader (or a future enforce-mode flip) would trust incorrectly.

findings.desc: story-aware-validation.ts discoverValidationInventory (F-441 fix, a89e174746): the no-config-file-at-all case now reports the wrong source filename. New code: picked = pickProjectConfigPath(projectRoot); source = picked?.legacy ? DEPRECATED_CONFIG_FILENAME : PROOF_OR_STOP_CONFIG_FILENAME. pickProjectConfigPath returns null when neither proof-or-stop.config.json nor lattice.config.json exists (verified live via node -e against compiled dist on an empty temp dir -> null). null?.legacy is undefined/falsy, so source resolves to the CANONICAL name in that branch. OLD code (pre-fix): source: existsSync(join(projectRoot, "proof-or-stop.config.json")) ? canonical : legacy -- when neither file exists, existsSync(canonical) is false, so the OLD ternary fell through to the LEGACY name (lattice.config.json). So the no-config-file case flipped which filename is reported (legacy before the fix, canonical after) -- a genuine behavior discrepancy from the fix, not covered by the original F-441 text (which only addressed the join()+existsSync ternary and the second existsSync probe, not this specific neither-file-exists edge). Impact assessed as low: grepped all consumers of ValidationInventory.source across packages/main/src and packages/main/tests -- zero call sites branch on inventory.source; it is purely informational metadata in the returned object. Unreachable in this repo today since proof-or-stop.config.json is always present at project root. No existing test exercises the non-injected file-lookup branch at all (story-aware-validation-smoke.ts and friends all pass injected commands, short-circuiting source to the injected literal), so this was never guarded either before or after the fix. Recommend: either document source=canonical-on-no-config-file as the new intended default, or add an explicit no-config-file branch preserving legacy semantics for parity, plus a regression test for the neither-file-exists case.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 8d605caeba. Restored explicitly with picked ? (picked.legacy ? DEPRECATED : CANONICAL) : DEPRECATED. Verified live against a fresh empty temp dir before and after: reports lattice.config.json again, matching pre-F-441 behaviour, while the real repo still reports proof-or-stop.config.json with 112 commands. Independently reproduced by lattice-review-concept and by lattice-review-quality, the latter diffing against a89e174746 to recover the original logic.

findings.desc: The validation runtime tracer child_process wrapper (validation-runtime-tracer.cjs:123-131) replaces execFile with a bare wrapper function that does not carry over util.promisify.custom or other own properties of the original. Any traced descendant that uses util.promisify(execFile) silently gets the generic promisify fallback, which resolves with the bare stdout string instead of {stdout, stderr}. Concrete failure: run-proofstory-acceptance-rollout-cohort.mjs:168-182 destructures {stdout: output} from the resolved value, output becomes undefined, and .split throws TypeError, aborting the root full test suite (npm test 0/58) under done_required_validate while the identical suite passes 58/58 without the tracer. Reproduced deterministically by running proofstory-acceptance-rollout-smoke.js with NODE_OPTIONS=--require .../validation-runtime-tracer.cjs. Fix: copy own property descriptors (at minimum the util.promisify.custom symbol) from the original child_process function onto each wrapper so the tracer is transparent to promisify, plus a regression test that asserts promisify(execFile) still resolves {stdout, stderr} under the tracer.
